mark.shape: termination object of a directory entry: indicator (TERMINATED, ACTIVE or UNKNOWN) and effective_date (an ISO day); the source-removed marker travels as a cohort.capability_facts string source_removed_on=<date>
mark.owner: directory refresh Lambda: lambda_handler in directory/refresh.py (the scheduled fire) calls resolve_disappeared, which calls carry_forward_terminated

precedent.how_set: both TERMINATED entries carry the source_removed_on capability fact, so the writer's carry-forward rule set the mark (absent from the build and from the source snapshot); the source marks the other 269 entries UNKNOWN

evidence.statement: The custodian source lists the account with two rows carrying no position on each of these four trading days, and its independent-total partitions hold no row for it on any of them; the last trading day with a nonzero independent total is 2026-10-08.

offline_guard.invocation: python -I step6_offline.py (scratch script outside the repository): build_snapshot, then the HEAD evaluate_publish_gate with a stub closed-account provider

candidate_vs_served.reading: The two dates differ by two trading days, so amounts move on 16764 of 17800 compared nodes and 148 nodes appear or disappear. The acceptance itself removes only the one account's 3 nodes; the rest of the difference comes from the dates and is not attributed to the acceptance.

cottonwood.statement: The deployed directory_marks_no_closures has no carried-forward exclusion, while HEAD ignores the pipeline's own TERMINATED marks. With the two carried entries present it returns False, so the deployed gate refuses the lost account (executed: REFUSED, account_lost 1) where HEAD lists it and publishes.

49financial.statement: The deployed 49 Financial file is another version (3241 lines against HEAD 3290). Its evaluate_publish_gate equals HEAD, and its directory_marks_no_closures has the same no-carried-exclusion body as the Cottonwood bundle (AST comparison, not executed on the 49 Financial directory).

rollback.statement: The prior accepted publication is the served index at business date 2026-10-08 (index version in the notes); it returns by re-pointing the current index to that version id. Nothing is deleted, and this order wrote nothing.
